author: Roger Anderson
title: Poll: Trust in Politics Collapses - NewsBreak
text:
By Roger Anderson ,
7 hours ago A Siena/New York Times poll has revealed that only one-third of Americans now believe the political system can heal divisions, a sharp decline from over half in 2020. Analysts said the shift is a result of widespread anxiety over the nation’s ability to overcome partisan divides. Polarization now ranks just behind the economy as a top voter concern, up from under 1% before the last election.
Rep. Steve Scalise (R-LA) said, “There’s no excuse for political violence in our country, it’s got to end.” He added, “It’s a problem that we’ve seen grow and it’s got to be addressed. It’s got to stop.”
Only 55% say the U.S. is still a democracy, while 41% disagree. Fears over democracy have significantly grown following the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk.
Johns Hopkins University professor Ruth Braunstein stated that Kirk’s death “is obviously a tragedy on a personal level, but it also does have the capacity to further inflame a political environment where the temperature is already way too high. That’s a real possibility, and a real risk.”
30% now believe violence may be needed to restore order. Despite this, most do not see political opponents as enemies.
President Donald Trump said, “Violence and murder are the tragic consequence of demonizing those with whom you disagree – day after day, year after year – in the most hateful and despicable way possible.”
Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) stated, “Every single person who encourages aggressive responses to it rather than civil discourse owns a certain amount of responsibility for his death and anyone else’s.”
Roger Anderson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
